r1_shirorekha_final_final.judge: I looked at every listed image for both finalists and their pre-polish folders,
r1_shirorekha_final_final.what_works:
The idea is visible without a caption. One heavy line carries VANINDRA, steps down to a hairline over CREATIONS, becomes the 1 px page rule in the 1440 header with the navigation hanging from it, and steps up again in the Reel credit. 'Headline = the first three seconds' is a real business pun, and the drawing shows it.

The व mark is now correct as a letter. The loop leaves the danda as a 5.5 hairline and never touches the line, so it cannot be read as प. The line overhangs 3 units on each side, so T5's lopsided bar and the acute white sliver are gone. The SVG is four cubics and straight lines, crisp at every size. mark_small holds at 16 px (fav_x3.png): bar, pointed counter and stem all survive, and it is the strongest favicon either finalist has.

VANINDRA is a coherent drawn alphabet. Dandas are the verticals and leaves are the diagonals. The N stems are thinner than the N diagonal, so NIN no longer reads as a picket fence. The sturdy cut at a 28 px cap and the pixel-fitted 17 px phone cut both read cleanly (r1_hdr_desk_x4.png, r1_hdr_phone_x6.png).

CREATIONS is drawn from the same constructors: contrast-pen C and S, a leaf A and R, a superellipse O. Its proportions match VANINDRA, and the S is a single clean stroke at 4000 px (r1_creations.png).

The Devanagari uses the same pen and leaf rules.

The polish improved the system as a whole: CREATIONS is on the baseline, EDIT BY is drawn, the Reel line starts on the safe margin, and the header has real optical cuts.
must_fix: Lockup and header: the hairline over CREATIONS floats about 0.42 of VANINDRA's cap (about 0.76 of CREATIONS' own cap) above the CREATIONS tops (r1_creations.png). It reads as an overline hovering over a separate word, which contradicts 'everything hangs from one line'. Either end the line at the last A of VANINDRA and let CREATIONS stand free, or close the gap to about 0.15 cap.

Mark master: the loop's left shoulder is about 15 units thick (outer x 19 vs inner x 34 at y 56-59), heavier than the 13-unit danda. The eye lands on the bowl's knuckle, not the stem, and at 40-56 px the bowl + stem + bar reads as a Latin 'a' under a macron (avatars_small_x3.png). Take the shoulder to about 12 so the danda is the heaviest stroke. The pre-polish round bowl was more graceful; keep the point, but open the shoulder radius so it stops looking like a blade.

Global avatar (mark_global_on_emerald): at 32-40 px the full-bleed gold bar becomes a chord across the circle, and the V's hairline right arm thins to about 1 px. What reads is a wedge under a rule, close to a ∇ or a dropdown caret (gav_x5.png). Give the 32-48 px cut a right arm of at least 2 px, or use the sturdy VANINDRA wordmark in the circle for USD accounts.

Reel credit: EDIT BY has 2.2 px stems at a 10.5 px cap, while VANINDRA's sturdy hairlines in the same tag render at about 1 px. The label is visibly darker than the name it credits and looks like a stock bold grotesque (r1_reel_x4.png). Bring EDIT BY down to about 1.4 px stems.

वनिंद्रा: every Devanagari outline is a sampled polyline (414 straight 'L' segments in wordmark_devanagari.svg), so facets will show in large print and signage. The द्र drop, the ि hook length and the anusvara position still need native sign-off. Redraw as béziers after the native review.

Master VANINDRA: the A apexes are flat-cut into the 8.8-unit bar across a full-cap Latin word. At display size this 'roof' is still the closest thing in the round to the Samarkan register. Make the gold-hairline version (global.svg) the default outside India and on any surface larger than about 300 mm.

r1_shirorekha_final_final.judge: I judged as two people: a lifestyle creator with 4 lakh followers deciding on Rs
r1_shirorekha_final_final.what_works: The idea is visible in every drawing: one line that the name, the credit and the website navigation hang from. It is austere enough to stay clear of the Samarkan/restaurant look. The leaf diagonals (hairline at the line, full weight at the foot) and the superellipse D/R give VANINDRA a recognisable voice that reads like a modern Indian couture label, which suits jewellery and saree brand partners. Versus T5: CREATIONS is now drawn in the same system (flared C/S, leaf A/R, superellipse O) and sits on VANINDRA's baseline. The horizontal lockup no longer repeats the initial. The bar overhang is balanced, and the danda runs past the loop's point, so at 16 px it reads as a letter, not a funnel or pennant. The व avatar is the strongest small-size asset in Round 3: the counter triangle survives at 16-24 px and it fills the 110 px circle well. The 17 px phone cut is crisp and the NIN cluster no longer turns into a barcode at a 28 px cap. The global gold-hairline wordmark (caps overlapping the line) is a quiet, credible version for USD clients. The Reel credit ('EDIT BY' on a hairline, then VANINDRA under its bar) looks like a film credit, not a watermark, and I would be proud to carry it. The polish improved on r1_shirorekha_final: the pointed bowl shows a V counter instead of a soft round 'a', CREATIONS is no longer a superscript, and the EDIT BY credit went from illegible to clear.
must_fix: Global avatar (mark_global_on_*.svg, context_global.png): the V is a plain wedge hanging from a bar. At 32 px it reads as a ▼ dropdown or filter icon, and at 110 px the full-bleed bar plus wedge reads as a coat hanger or a 'T'. This is the lone default V that Round 2 banned. Give it the व's DNA: the swelling left shoulder that tapers to a hairline, a sharp point, and a short danda stub on the right below the line, so it is the system's letter and not a generic initial.

Mark outer shoulder at (2,40): at 900 px tall it is a blunt round knuckle about 110 px wide set against a knife-straight return stroke. In the 110 px gold-on-emerald avatar, the closed loop plus right stem reads to non-Hindi eyes as a single-storey 'a' under a bar ('ā'). Tighten the shoulder radius and taper it toward the 5.5 hairline so the triangular counter, the V, dominates the silhouette.

wordmark_devanagari.svg / bilingual lockup: the द्र rakar is a large inverted-V caret. At 1000 px width it drops about 75 units below the baseline (y≈445-595 against a baseline of 520), the heaviest and lowest shape in the word, and it pulls the eye away from व. Reduce it to a short diagonal crossing the द's tail, inside about 40% of that depth. The न's left element is a teardrop tucked under the mid-bar (x≈435-475, y≈360-420), not a descending stroke, and reads as a stray blob. Native sign-off on द्र, the ि hook length and the anusvara before any public use.

lockup_stacked_on_*.svg: CREATIONS floats under VANINDRA with no line to hang from. This breaks the 'everything hangs from one line' rule that the horizontal lockup keeps, and the stacked lockup looks like a different system. Hang it from a hairline, as in the horizontal lockup.

reel_tag.png: at 540×960 the bar over VANINDRA is about 2 px, barely heavier than the 1 px EDIT BY hairline, so the step up to the heavy bar, which is the credit's idea, can't be seen at Reel size. The V and A left hairlines are about 1.2 px over dark hair. Use the sturdy cut and make the bar at least 2× the hairline in the credit file.

Pan-India: the only primary avatar is a Devanagari letter. Tamil Nadu and Karnataka creators will read it as a Hindi-belt studio, and Bengali readers will read it as ব. Once the global line-V is redrawn (first item), approve it as the avatar for South Indian outreach as well as for the USD workspace.

r1_shirorekha_final_final.judge: I judged as two people: a US B2B founder deciding whether to pay an offshore stu
r1_shirorekha_final_final.what_works:
The new व mark fixes T5's lean.
- The pointed bowl leaves the danda as a hairline, swells to a shoulder at the far left and ends in a sharp point. This fills the bottom-left quadrant that the Round 2 judges called empty.
- The bar now overhangs equally at both ends.
- The counter is a clean downward triangle, and the curves are smooth with no wobble.
- At 16 px (pixel dump) it still has an open counter, a 2 px danda and a visible point. That is the most distinctive favicon in either round.

The wordmark's thin-at-the-line, heavy-at-the-foot leaf diagonals are ownable without a story. The line does real work: it becomes the 1 px page rule that the website navigation hangs from, and it runs unbroken over VANINDRA and वनिंद्रा in the bilingual lockup. That shared line is the most ownable asset in three rounds.

The global lockup reads like a serious international studio: one gold hairline, caps touching it, CREATIONS drawn in the system and sitting on the baseline.

The polish clearly improved the pre-polish version:
- The rounder, 'd'-like bowl became the sharper V-counter bowl.
- The superscript CREATIONS (which looked stuck on) now sits on the baseline.
- The stacked lockups now show the full name.
- The Reel credit has a proper margin.

One-colour versions hold. At 1-bit, 40 px, the master's top hairline survives.
must_fix: Global avatar (mark_global_on_emerald): in the 110 px circle, the full-bleed bar is cut into a chord by the circle edge. At 32-40 px it thins to a 1 px gold line, leaving a bare down-pointing triangle that reads as a dropdown or download chevron. It is the 'decorated V' Round 2 banned. Draw a small cut with a heavier bar, and make the V's thin-to-thick leaf arm show at 40 px.

mark_small at 16 px is not pixel-fitted. The bar's left end and the danda's right edge fall off the pixel grid, leaving grey columns at 30-50% on both sides (pixel values 77 and 119/56 of 241). The bowl's top stroke lands as one half-grey row (73-137). Hand-hint the 16 and 32 px ICO so the danda is exactly 2 px and the bowl's top lands on a full row.

Reel credit (reel_tag.png, 540 wide): the step from the hairline under EDIT BY up to the bar over VANINDRA is only about 1 px, so it reads as an uneven rule rather than a deliberate step. At about 17 px cap height over the photo, VANINDRA's hairline V right arm and A left leg break up against the hair texture. Make the step at least 2x the hairline, or use the sturdy cut in the credit.

Full-name lockup (lockup_horizontal_header): the hairline over CREATIONS floats about half a cap-height above the caps. CREATIONS is therefore the one element that does not hang from the line, and at the 28 px header the gap looks accidental rather than designed.

Bilingual lockup: the रकार (r-sign) in द्र is two strokes crossing into an X or λ under the द bowl, instead of a short caret hanging from the द's tail. The ि hook thins to a hairline that vanishes before it reaches the न's danda once the lockup is 160 px wide. A native reader must sign off before any public use.

Header sturdy cut: at 28 px cap the bar is about 3 px over 16-unit stems. The heavy overline over all-caps is where the 'Indian menu' (Samarkan-style) look comes closest; check it beside the gold-hairline global version before choosing the default header.

r3_hinge.judge: I looked at every listed image for both finalists and their pre-polish folders,
r3_hinge.what_works:
The polish fixed the fatal misread. The pre-polish nI ligature read as 'Varlndra' or 'Vanndra' in the header and the avatar. The staircase reads 'Van / Indra' at every header size, 44 px tall included (r3_hdr_phone_x5.png).

The join is visible in the drawing: the n's right leg lands on the gold I's head serif. Mapping the gold I to the gold ि in वनिंद्रा is a genuinely clever cross-script rhyme, and you can see it in the bilingual lockup without being told.

The Reel credit (lowercase 'edit by' over a small staircase) is the most editorial and least watermark-like tag of the round (r3_reel_x4.png).

At use sizes the lowercase has believable contrast and one consistent knife-cut terminal. The whole thing reads as a premium editorial studio to a London or New York client, so it is the better of the two global wordmarks.

The Devanagari follows the Latin pen: heavy dandas, a light shirorekha, knife-cut ends.
must_fix: Favicon (mark_small.svg / mark_small_tile.svg): this is a stock-looking Didone V with bracketed slabs. At 16 px it is a plain 'v' with no trace of the hinge (fav_x3.png), which is exactly the lone V Round 2 told everyone to stop making. Draw the small mark from the join itself: the emerald n leg landing on the gold I head, cut heavy for 48 px and below.

d: the d is about 80% of the n's width, and its counter is about 65% of the n's counter, a straight-sided slot. The flat left wall meets the bottom curve at a visible corner (r3_d.png). It is the darkest, most condensed letter in 'ndra'. Widen it to the n's width and redraw the counter as one continuous oval.

One-line wordmark: the gold I is drawn ascender-tall and stands about 3% above the V's cap line, level with the d's ascender (r3_wm_big.png). Two capitals sit at two heights. Cut the I to cap height in wordmark / wordmark_small / wordmark_mono. Only the staircase needs the ascender-tall I.

Staircase: the I's foot serif ends about 12 units from the n's left foot serif (about 0.8% of the lockup width, versus 25-30 units for the other letter gaps) (r3_stair_big.png). In the 56-110 px avatar the two feet fuse into one slab under 'In'. Open this gap to match the n-d gap.

'Creations' (58%, heavier cut): its C stem is about 35 px where a matching optical cut would give about 25 px, so it is roughly 40% heavier per unit than 'Indra' (global.png). The descriptor is darker than the name it qualifies, and the e's eye and the s spine clog. Use about +10% optical compensation, not +40%.

Avatar (mark_on_emerald): eight letters in a circle. At 56 px the x-height is about 5 px and the soft-gold I on emerald is a faint stripe. At 32-40 px it is a grey texture (r3_ctx_av56_x5.png, avatars_small_x3.png). For a business whose front door is Instagram, this needs a drawn avatar built from the hinge, not the name set small.

The join: the gold I head is wider than the emerald n stem and bracketed on both sides, so at 1:1 it reads as an emerald post standing in a gold collar (r3_join.png). That is two strokes stacked, which contradicts the 'one stroke for two words' story. Either carry the gold up into the n's leg, or rewrite the story. Also, the gold singles out 'Indra' as a separate, highlighted name, which invites 'who is Indra?'. Tell the public story as forest + sky only, per the brief's rule on the name.

r3_hinge.judge: I judged as two people: a lifestyle creator with 4 lakh followers deciding on Rs
r3_hinge.what_works: A clean, consistent editorial serif: one knife-cut terminal rule across a, r, s, C, e and t, bracketed slabs, and no wobbly béziers in the n arches or the V. The staircase 'Van / Indra' with the gold I is elegant at header size (64 px desktop, 44 px phone). The 'edit by / Van Indra' Reel credit reads like a fashion-magazine credit, which a skincare or beauty D2C manager would accept straight away. It is the most comfortable of the two for London or New York clients, and it is Latin-first with optional Devanagari, so it is easy to use pan-India, including Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. The bilingual insight, that n plus the gold I equals नि and its gold ि, is genuinely clever. The polish clearly improved on r3_hinge: the pre-polish one-line ligature read 'Van'ndra' or 'VarIndra', and its n-I avatar read as 'nl' or a mirrored h. The staircase fixes the misreading and Creations is now drawn in the same pen. The cost is that the 'one stroke, two letters' idea now shows only as a vertical alignment in the two-line version. The one-line wordmark is just a serif VanIndra with a gold I.
must_fix: Avatar at Instagram's real sizes: the staircase in mark_on_ivory/emerald becomes a grey texture at 32-40 px. In context.png the second and third circles show an x-height of about 3 px, and those are the comment, story and DM sizes where an Instagram studio is seen most. At 48 px and below, mark_small.svg is a stock-looking bracketed Didone V, the font-letter move the owner called the worst in Round 1. An ownable small mark drawn from the hinge is needed, for example the emerald stem dropping into the gold crossguard slab seen in the join zoom.

The gold I vanishes on warm or bright backgrounds. In reel_tag_dark.png the soft-gold I over the lamp-lit peach wall has almost no contrast and the credit reads 'Van ndra'. On ivory the antique-gold I is visibly lighter than the emerald letters at the 44 px phone header. Give photos an ivory I (or a darker gold) and a contrast rule.

Bilingual lockup: the gold I (x≈535-570 at 1100 px) and the gold ि stem (x≈445-470) are about 90 px out of alignment, so the one bilingual idea isn't shown. वनिंद्रा's dandas (about 40 px) are much heavier than VanIndra's stems (about 25 px), so the Devanagari line reads darker and louder than the name. Align the two golds vertically and lighten the Devanagari to match.

Devanagari drawing: the ि hook leaves its stem with a lumpy, walking-stick kink (at 1100 px, x≈315-375, y≈20-140) and ends in mid-air above the shirorekha. The द्र rakar is an oversized crossing 'X' that hangs about 75 px below the baseline and outweighs the rest of the word. Native sign-off required.

d of Indra (wordmark at 1400 px, x≈1000-1050): the counter has a hard angular top-left corner and a sharp spur at the bottom-left where it meets the stem. This is out of step with the round n arches and shows at display sizes.

Name split: on its own line, 'Van' reads to global clients as the English vehicle word. Isolating 'Indra' as a separate capitalised word, picked out in gold, puts heavy emphasis on the name having two parts, while the brief says to never imply who else the name comes from. The owner should consciously sign off on this before a vote.

r3_hinge.judge: I judged as two people: a US B2B founder deciding whether to pay an offshore stu
r3_hinge.what_works:
The letterforms are the most refined of the three rounds:
- One rising knife cut on every terminal of a, r, s, C, e, t and y.
- Bracketed slab feet and a well-spaced 'Van'.
- The I is exactly the ascender's height.

The staircase header and the 'edit by / Van / Indra' Reel credit look like a London or New York boutique studio. A US client would find them premium and immediately legible.

The polish fixed the pre-polish one-line ligature, which misread as 'Varlndra' and 'Van'ndra' at every size. The Reel credit now switches to all-emerald on light footage, which is the right production call.

The Devanagari is credible and the gold ि echo is a neat bilingual touch: a round-bowl व, a wedge on न and heavy dandas.
must_fix: Favicon and app icon (mark_small.svg): bracketed slab serifs, a heavy left arm and a hairline right arm. That is the anatomy of any Bodoni or Playfair V, and at 16 px nothing ties it to the gold I or the hinge. It is the lone default V that Round 2 banned and the owner already rejected. Draw a small mark from the system itself, for example the emerald stem standing on the gold I-slab as one two-colour stroke.

The Instagram avatar (mark_on_emerald.svg) is the two-line staircase. In the 110 px circle the cap height is only about 18 px, and the top-right and bottom-left of the circle are empty. At 40 and 32 px the counters of a, n, d and r close and it becomes a grey smudge with one gold dash. Instagram uses one image at every size, so comments, story rings and collab tags (the lead-gen engine) show no brand.

The hinge join (staircase, 3x): the colour changes at the top of the shared slab. The n loses its foot, and the gold brackets flare up around the emerald stem like a sword's crossguard or a collar. The 'one stroke' therefore reads as a gold I with an n set on top of it. Either drop the colour break to the underside of the slab or run the gold up into the n's leg.
The one-line wordmark (wordmark_small 'VanIndra') has no hinge left, only a gold I. Every email signature, invoice and deck footer loses the concept.
Splitting the name as 'Van' over 'Indra', with Indra's I in gold, invites people to read the name as two personal names joined together. The brief forbids implying who the name comes from.

Devanagari: the रकार (r-sign) of द्र is a heavy diagonal crossing a thin one under the bowl. The knife-cut feet on the व and ा dandas look chipped. The ि hook ends in a cut above the line. Native verification is needed.
Embroidery: the small-cut hairline (34 units against a 700 cap) needs at least 90 mm of width, so caps, sleeves and pocket marks fall back to the generic V.
